response.why: Playing Undercity Sewers is superior to passing. Pass leaves me vulnerable: opponent's Anoint with Affliction (leaf 1: 30/100) removes one of my creatures while I only have 2 mana next turn, crippling the draw engine strategy. Playing Sewers provides three land sources (Swamp + 2x Sewers untapped) for next turn, enabling Preacher of the Schism {2}{B} deployment despite opponent disruption. Even against dangerous threats like Kaito (leaves 4-5) or additional Preachers (leaves 6-7), the mana setup is critical. Leaf 8 (Anoint after Sewers) is still dangerous but less crippling since I'm 3-lands-strong next turn, versus pass's 2-land constraint. Mana development is non-negotiable for the core strategy.
response.plan: Play Undercity Sewers (third land enters tapped; Sewers enters untapped next turn per normal untap). Main phase nearly complete. Next turn, turn 8: untap all three lands (2x Sewers + Swamp untapped), generating {B}{B}{B}. Cast Preacher of the Schism {2}{B} to establish draw engine parity. Board state becomes Faerie 2/1 + Bat 1/1 + Preacher 2/4 (3 threats across 3 land mana). Even if opponent plays removal or threats, I'm positioned for the draw race grind toward Sheoldred, The Apocalypse finisher. Life totals remain 18 vs 20—maintain focus on resource accumulation.

response.why: Attacking with Faerie is critical to establish life parity. Leaf 1 shows unblocked 2-damage attack, bringing opponent from 20 to 18 (matching my life total). This parity is essential for next turn's draw engine strategy. Preacher of the Schism's ability triggers when I have most/tied life: "create token, draw card, lose 1 life." At 18-18 parity, deploying my Preacher next turn guarantees draw triggers. Without attack (leaf 0), opponent stays at 20 life—my Preacher wouldn't trigger on attack (opponent has more), losing card advantage. The symmetric draw race requires parity. Passing (35/100) abandons the core strategy; attacking (85/100) purchases the draw advantage that leads to Sheoldred victory condition.
response.plan: Attack with Faerie Mastermind. Faerie deals 2 unblocked damage (opponent: 20→18). Establish parity: both players at 18 life. Faerie taps. Turn 8 main phase: draw 1 land if available (Sewers from hand), generate {B}{B}{B} from 3 lands. Cast Preacher of the Schism {2}{B}. Board: Faerie (tapped) + Bat + Preacher. Turn 8 combat: attack with both Faerie and Preacher while at parity (18-18). Both Preachers trigger: create Vampire tokens, draw cards, lose 1 life each (reach 16 life). Opponent Preacher also triggers at parity. Draw race accelerates. Continue grinding toward Sheoldred finisher where card draw converts to life swing.

response.why: No blocks allows opponent damage but preserves both my creatures for future turns. Bat blocking Drowner is the optimal trade—removes their evasive threat while Bat's summoning sickness makes it ineffective anyway. Bat blocking Preacher wastes the block since Preacher is tapped and Bat is still summoning sick.
response.plan: Allow Bat to block Drowner (optimal trade). Execute turn 8 main phase: play Undercity Sewers for third land, cast Preacher of the Schism to establish parity draw engine. Attack with Faerie + Preacher at parity (18-18) next combat to trigger symmetric draws and start grinding toward Sheoldred finisher.

response.why: Casting Floodpits Drowner ({1}{U}) in upkeep depletes my limited mana sources. With only Swamp + 2 Undercity Sewers (3 total sources), casting Floodpits leaves me 1 source short of the {2}{B} required for Preacher of the Schism in main phase. Passing + doing nothing (leaves 2, 5, 8) preserves full mana for my core strategy. Even Leaf 8 (opponent casts Sheoldred) is preferable to being unable to deploy Preacher—Sheoldred's draw punishment is damaging but I can still execute the symmetric parity engine. Responding with Floodpits in any scenario (leaves 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7) blocks my main win condition entirely.
response.plan: Pass priority. Proceed to main phase with full mana. Cast Preacher of the Schism to establish parity draw engine (18-18). Attack with both Faerie Mastermind and Preacher on turn 9 combat, triggering simultaneous draws/tokens. Build toward Sheoldred deployment turn 10-11 as finisher converting draw race to life swing.

response.why: Cast Preacher of the Schism is optimal. Deploying it immediately establishes the parity draw engine (17-17 life), triggering on turn 9 combat to generate cards and Vampire tokens. This is the core win condition and must execute now. Pass leaves (0-14) are inferior because they defer deployment—I either respond with Floodpits (depletes mana, leaves 0-3, 5-8, 10-13 scored 20) or do nothing (full mana but Preacher delayed, leaves 4/9/14 scored 65). Play Undercity Sewers (15-29) defers Preacher further; only 'do nothing' leaves (19, 29) score well (60-65), and Leaf 24 is catastrophic (Cut Down destroys my Faerie, 10/100). Cast Preacher (30-35) scores 50-65: Sheoldred responses (30, 32) are concerning but manageable (50); benign responses (31, 33-35) score 55-65. Cast Floodpits (36-41) prevents Preacher deployment entirely (25 all).
response.plan: Cast Preacher of the Schism immediately to deploy draw engine at parity. Attack turn 9 combat with Faerie Mastermind + Preacher, triggering both at life parity (17-17) for simultaneous card draws, Vampire tokens, and 1-life cost each. response.why: Pass with 'do nothing' response (leaves 4, 9, 14) scores 50/100—preserves full mana {U}{U}{B}, {U}{B}{B}, {B}{B}{B} for critical Sheoldred the Apocalypse cast during main phase. Sheoldred ({2}{B}{B}) is the ONLY viable win condition now: original Preacher parity strategy broken due to life differential (I'm at 10 life, opponent at 16—Preacher no longer attacks 'player with most life'). Pass with forced Floodpits responses (0-3, 5-8, 10-13) scores 15/100—mana depletes to {U}{B}, preventing Sheoldred deployment. Cast Floodpits (all leaves) scores 15-25/100—consumes critical mana, blocks Sheoldred finisher. Cast Cut Down (all leaves) scores 25-35/100—cheaper cost preserves some mana but still consumes resources before main phase.
response.plan: Pass priority at upkeep, preserving full mana to reach main phase. Execute Sheoldred the Apocalypse ({2}{B}{B}) cast immediately—this is the new win condition. Sheoldred converts the draw race into a direct damage engine: each opponent card draw costs them 2 life, each my card draw gains me 2 life. With Faerie Mastermind and existing board presence generating card draws, Sheoldred on board converts this into a 4-life swing per card drawn, winning from 10 life. Critical: do not expend mana during upkeep.

response.why: Pass preserves maximum strategic flexibility and mana availability (3 untapped lands = full mana pool access). Key scenario analysis: (1) Opponent frequently deploys Sheoldred if I play land (leaves 15-29, many Sheoldred casts), creating devastating draw-race where opponent gains 2 life per draw and I lose 2, which is losing from 10 life. (2) Passing and doing nothing (leaves 4, 9, 14) scores 70 by preserving full mana + hand size for responsive plays. (3) Reactive spell casts after opponent deploys (leaves 0-3, 5-8, 10-13, etc) score 40-45: I burn mana but Faerie Mastermind remains active. (4) Casting Preacher/Floodpits/Cut Down proactively taps resources and doesn't address Sheoldred threat. (5) Playing Undercity Sewers triggers opponent's aggressive responses (high Sheoldred incidence), scoring 15-45. (6) Cut Down deployments score 45-55 similarly to first Floodpits option but consume colored mana inefficiently.
response.plan: Pass priority and force opponent's hand. Standing position: opponent at 16 life vs my 10 life (critical). Sheoldred the Apocalypse (2BB, 4/5 in hand) is my finisher but requires 4 mana this turn (only have 3 untapped). Core strategy: preserve mana + full hand to respond after opponent commits resources. If opponent casts their Sheoldred, I'm forced into losing draw race (opponent +2 life per draw, me -2). By passing, I signal flexibility and create windows to answer their Sheoldred with mine on next turn when I untap the 4th land. This plan holds until opponent commits to Sheoldred; if they deploy other threats, I can respond with Floodpits/Cut Down from retained mana.

response.why: Begin Combat phase occurs after Main Phase 1 (which I passed) but BEFORE Main Phase 2. This is critical: only Flash creatures and instants are castable now (Floodpits Drowner, Cut Down); Sheoldred the Apocalypse requires Main Phase 2 with {2}{B}{B} mana. Key observation: opponent's untapped creatures (Preacher, Floodpits Drowner, Vampire Tokens) all have summoning sickness and CANNOT attack this turn. Their tapped creatures cannot attack. Zero combat damage incoming this turn. Therefore, Begin Combat priority should optimize for Main Phase 2 options, not defense. Mana math: with {U}{B}{B} available, I can cast Sheoldred if I preserve full mana pool (generic costs pay {U} + {B}, black requirements pay remaining {B}{B}). Casting Floodpits or Cut Down now consumes mana, preventing Sheoldred deployment in Main 2. Pass with full mana preservation scores 70 (leaves 4, 9, 14: do-nothing scenarios where I keep {U}{B}{B} available for Sheoldred). Reactive spell casting scores 40-45 (burns mana, foils finisher window). Opponent deploying Sheoldred on their turn (leaves 18-20, 43-47) scores 15-25: they resolve the finisher before I get Main Phase 2 window, trapping me in losing draw race.
response.plan: Pass priority to preserve {U}{B}{B} mana for Sheoldred casting in Main Phase 2. Standing position: opponent has no creatures capable of attacking (all untapped creatures summoning sick, all tapped creatures cannot swing). Combat creates no immediate threats. My finisher (Sheoldred, 4/5, {2}{B}{B}) is castable this turn if mana preserved. Deploy Sheoldred in upcoming Main Phase 2 to establish the draw-race engine (Sheoldred + Faerie Mastermind triggers = 4-life swing per draw: opponent -2, me +2). Plan holds if opponent doesn't deploy their own Sheoldred first (which they might, given they have 4+ mana available in some scenarios). If opponent casts Sheoldred before my Main Phase 2, abandon finisher window and shift to tempo/survival strategy for next turn.

response.why: Attack-all (dealing 2 damage with Faerie Mastermind) is strongly favored. Faerie has flying and is unblocked (opponent's untapped creatures all have summoning sickness, tapped creatures cannot block). The 2-point damage directly advances the win condition by moving life totals from 10 vs 16 to 10 vs 14. Critical strategic insight: Sheoldred the Apocalypse (in hand, {2}{B}{B} mana available via {U}{B}{B} pool) creates an exponential draw-race engine. Sheoldred triggers on EVERY draw: (1) Opponent draws card 1 → opponent loses 2 life; (2) Opponent draws card 2 → opponent loses 2 life, AND Faerie Mastermind triggers my draw; (3) When I draw → I gain 2 life. Per turn life swing: opponent loses 4 (from their 2 draws), I gain 2 (from my 1 draw) = 6-point swing in my favor per turn. From 10 vs 14 after this attack, Sheoldred deployment in Main Phase 2 creates: Turn 1: me 12 vs opponent 10 (I'm ahead). This makes opponent's life total nearly irrelevant. Tapping Faerie to deal 2 damage is worthwhile because the draw-race engine eliminates need for blocking defense. Attack-none (45) is passive: preserves Faerie's untapped status and defensive blocking, but wastes tempo and doesn't advance toward inevitable draw-race victory.
response.plan: Attack with Faerie Mastermind, dealing 2 damage (16→14 opponent life). Preserve {U}{B}{B} mana for Sheoldred the Apocalypse deployment in Main Phase 2. Once Sheoldred resolves, maintain the draw-race engine: opponent loses 4 life per turn (from drawing 2 cards triggering Sheoldred's opponent-draw ability twice), I gain 2 per turn (from Faerie-triggered draw). Life gap closes to parity at turn 1 post-Sheoldred, then I pull ahead. Primary win condition: execute Sheoldred finisher and ride the draw-race to victory. Faerie's block potential becomes irrelevant given Sheoldred's life-swing dominance.

response.why: Pass preserves full mana for Sheoldred—the critical finisher that transforms this into a favorable draw race where Sheoldred's life swing dominates. Leaves 4, 9, 14 show me ready to cast Sheoldred with full mana ({U}{U}{B}, {U}{B}{B}, {B}{B}{B}) after opponent taps resources. Casting Drowner or Cut Down now taps me out and either forces an awkward second-response (wasting mana) or leaves insufficient mana for Sheoldred, allowing opponent a chance to cast their own Sheoldred first (catastrophic—leaf 42 shows opponent's Sheoldred winning the race instead). Both creatures are tapped, so no attacks available regardless; the priority decision is purely about mana preservation.
response.plan: Hold full mana for post-combat Sheoldred deployment. Once Sheoldred is down, ride the draw-race: opponent draws 2 cards per turn (−4 life from Sheoldred), I draw once (from Faerie Mastermind on opponent's 2nd card draw), and Preacher triggers on attack (+draw if tied/lower life). The life gap closes quickly in my favor. Faerie + Sheoldred is an unstoppable two-card combo that wins from 10 life if I can resolve Sheoldred before opponent does.

response.why: Cut Down (worst leaf 25, best leaves 40/45/50 at 45) outperforms alternatives. Pass fatally allows opponent's Sheoldred online in many scenarios (leaves 0-3, 5-8: score 18), even when preserving mana (leaf 4/9: score 22 with opponent's Sheoldred draining). Ninjutsu is risky (leaf 17 loses Preacher to Go for the Throat). Cut Down's best outcomes (leaves 40, 45, 50) preserve full mana for Sheoldred post-combat while opponent plays non-Sheoldred spells, avoiding the race loss condition. Drowner taps out too completely (most leaves ~25).
response.plan: Cast Cut Down now to deny opponent's small threats and maximize likelihood of preserving enough mana ({U}{U}, {U}{B}, {B}{B} minimum) for Sheoldred deployment in post-combat main. The leaves show opponent more likely to play Faerie/Kaito/Preacher than Sheoldred after Cut Down, and I retain enough mana to cast Sheoldred before they establish their own. Once Sheoldred resolves before opponent's, the draw-race is won.

response.why: Floodpits Drowner (index 1) is the most problematic of available targets. It can block, has vigilance for re-use, and its ability taps my creatures with stun counters—directly interfering with my plan. The Vampire Tokens (indices 2, 3) are minor lifelink threats. Removing Floodpits Drowner preserves my board flexibility going into post-combat main phase when I need to deploy Sheoldred.
response.plan: Execute Cut Down on Floodpits Drowner. This clears one of opponent's defensive blockers before we move to post-combat main, where I'll cast Sheoldred with preserved mana. Once Sheoldred resolves, the draw-race engine activates (Sheoldred drains 2 per opponent draw, gains 2 per my draw via Faerie). My 10 life is survivable once Sheoldred is online and opponent at 16 life.

response.why: Game is lost at 4 life with no win path. Blocking strategies preserve life for another turn before lethal next turn. Leaf 0 (no-blocks): 4 damage unblocked → 0 life (dead immediately). Leaf 1-2, 4 (single Preacher or Floodpits block): absorb 2 damage → 2 life (survive, opponent untaps for lethal Turn 15). Leaf 3 (Floodpits + Cut Down): survive 2 life but lose Preacher blocker. Leaf 5-6 (Spyglass block): weaker blocker, survives. Leaf 7 (Preacher + Floodpits blocks): 4 life remaining despite Cut Down (best outcome). Leaf 8 (all blockers): 2 life. In terminal loss, maximum survival turns matter.
response.plan: Block with Preacher + Floodpits to maximize blockers and reach 4 life (or 2 life if Cut Down resolves). Game ends Turn 15 when opponent attacks again. This is the only remaining strategic goal in a lost position.

response.why: All outcomes end with opponent at 9 life (reduced from 11 by Sheoldred entering trigger when opponent drew card to cast). Passing (leaves 0-2, avg 18.7) preserves Spyglass Siren across all scenarios. Playing Swamp (leaves 3-5, avg 14.7) risks Siren removal via Cut Down (leaf 4, score 12) and trades immediate board for 1 potential mana. Leaf 4 is worst case—loses flyer while opponent gains Enduring Curiosity. Game remains terminal: opponent's Turn 15 Attack Phase with full board (~10 power) deals lethal to my 4 life regardless of action.
response.plan: Pass and hold defensive position with untapped creatures. Sheoldred creates mutual draw-penalty (opponent loses 2 when they draw; I gain 2 when I draw), which discourages opponent from card advantage. Lethal occurs on opponent's attack step. No action changes loss outcome; passing preserves board optionality.

response.why: All blocking scenarios result in lethal damage this turn. No-blocks (leaf 0): 8 unblocked damage brings me to -4 life (score 5). Blocking Enduring Curiosity 4/3 (leaf 1): Removes main threat, 4 remaining damage brings me to exactly 0 life (score 15, least overshoot). Blocking Preacher 2/4 (leaf 2): 6 remaining damage brings me to -2 (score 10). Blocking Vampire Token (leafs 3-4): 7 remaining damage brings me to -3 (score 8). All options result in game loss; blocking Enduring Curiosity minimizes excess life lost and is optimal in terminal position.
response.plan: Block Enduring Curiosity 4/3 with Sheoldred to minimize damage taken and reach exactly 0 life on opponent's attack. Game ends this turn regardless of blocking configuration; this option shows best defensive play by eliminating the largest threat, though outcome is death in all scenarios.
